questions.q:
Two narrow bores of diameter $5 . 0mm$ and $8 . 0mm$ are joined together to form a $U -$shaped tube open at both ends. If this $U -$tube contains water, what is the difference in the level of two limbs of the tube.
[Take surface tension of water $T = 7 . 3 \times {10}^{- 2}N{m}^{- 1}$, angle of contact $= 0, g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$ and density of water$\left= 1 . 0 \times {10}^{3}kg{m}^{- 3}\right]$
questions.solution:
${P}_{0} - \dfrac{2T}{{R}_{1}} + {h}_{1}ρg = {P}_{0} - \dfrac{2T}{{R}_{2}} + {h}_{2}ρg$
$\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right)ρg = 2T\left[\dfrac{1}{2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 3}} - \dfrac{1}{4 \times {10}^{- 3}}\right] ⇒ {h}_{1} - {h}_{2} = 2 . 19mm$

questions.q: Two small drops of mercury each of radius $R$ coalesce to form a single large drop. The ratio of total surface energy before and after the change is

questions.solution:

questions.q:
A water drop of radius $1cm$ is broken into $729$ equal droplets. If surface tension of water is $75dyne{cm}^{- 1}$, then the gain in surface energy upto first decimal place will be

[Given $\pi = 3 . 14$]
questions.solution:
The volume of the bigger drop will be, $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3}$. If the radius of smaller drops is $r$, using the conservation of volume,

$n\dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3} ⇒ 729 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{r}^{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi{R}^{3} ⇒ r = \dfrac{R}{9}$

The initial surface energy will be,

${E}_{i} = \left(4\pi{R}^{2}\right)T$

And final surface energy will be,

${E}_{f} = n\left(4\pi{r}^{2}\right)T = 729 \times 4\pi{\left(\dfrac{R}{9}\right)}^{2}T$$= 36\pi{R}^{2}T$

Therefore, the change in the surface energy will be,

$⇒ \DeltaE = {E}_{f} - {E}_{i} = 32\pi{R}^{2}T = 32 \times 3 . 14 \times {\left(1 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}^{2} \times 75 \times {10}^{- 3} ⇒ \DeltaE = 7 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}J$

questions.q: The velocity of a small ball of mass $m$ and density ${d}_{1}$, when dropped in a container filled with glycerine, becomes constant after some time. If the density of glycerine is ${d}_{2}$, then the viscous force acting on the ball, will be
questions.solution:
At the time of terminal velocity ball is in equilibrium i.e. ${F}_{g} = {F}_{b} + {F}_{v}$

$⇒ {F}_{v} = {F}_{g} - {F}_{b}$

$⇒ {F}_{v} = mg - {d}_{2}\dfrac{m}{{d}_{1}}g$

$⇒ mg\left(1 - \dfrac{{d}_{2}}{{d}_{1}}\right)$

questions.q: A pressure-pump has a horizontal tube of cross-sectional area $10{cm}^{2}$ for the outflow of water at a speed of $20m{s}^{- 1}$. The force exerted on the vertical wall just in front of the tube which stops water horizontally flowing out of the tube, is: [given : density of water $= 1000kg{m}^{- 3}$]
questions.solution:
Volume of water coming out of the pipe per sec $= Av = 10 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 20 = 0 . 02{m}^{3}{s}^{- 1}$

Mass of water hitting the wall per second $m = 0 . 02 \times {10}^{3} = 20kg{s}^{- 1}$

As the water hits the wall normal to the wall and stops, the change of momentum of water hitting the wall is $= m\left(0 - \left(- v\right)\right) = mv$

$= 20 \times 20 = 400kgm{s}^{- 2}$

Since, the change of momentum obtained is per unit time, it is same as the force.

Thus, the force acting on the wall by water $=$ force experienced by water jet$= 400N$.

questions.q:
Consider a cylindrical tank of radius $1m$ is filled with water. The top surface of water is at $15m$ from the bottom of the cylinder. There is a hole on the wall of cylinder at a height of $5m$ from the bottom. A force of $5 × {10}^{5}N$ is applied an the top surface of water using a piston. The speed of efflux from the hole will be :
(given atmospheric pressure ${P}_{A} = 1 . 01 × {10}^{5}Pa$, density of water ${ρ}_{w} = 1000kg{m}^{- 3}$ and gravitational acceleration $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Assuming there is no atmospheric pressure on piston, ${P}_{1} = \dfrac{F}{\pi{R}^{2}}$ and ${P}_{2} = {P}_{0}$.

Applying Bernoulli's equation at point $1$ and $2$,

${p}_{1} + ρg{h}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{1}^{2} = {p}_{2} + ρg{h}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{F}{\pi{R}^{2}}\right) + ρg\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right) = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2F}{\pi{R}^{2}ρ} - \dfrac{2{P}_{0}}{ρ} + 2g\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right)}$

${v}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times \left(5 \times {10}^{5}\right)}{3 . 14 \times {1}^{2} \times 1000} - \dfrac{2 \times 1 . 01 \times {10}^{5}}{1000} + 2 \times 10 \times 10}$

$\approx 17 . 8m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q: A small ball of mass $M$ and density $ρ$ is dropped in a viscous liquid of density ${ρ}_{0}$. After some time, the ball falls with a constant velocity. What is the viscous force on the ball?
questions.solution:
The buoyant force is given by

$B = V{ρ}_{0}g$

where $V$ is the volume of the ball. The weight of the ball

$W = Mg = Vρg$, is acting in the opposite direction of the buoyant force . Hence, at terminal velocity

$Mg - B = {F}_{v}$

$⇒ B + {F}_{v} = Mg$

$⇒ {F}_{v} = Vρg - V{ρ}_{0}g ⇒ {F}_{v} = ρVg ( 1 - \dfrac{{ρ}_{0}}{ρ} ) ⇒ {F}_{v} = Mg ( 1 - \dfrac{{ρ}_{0}}{ρ} )$

questions.q:
The figure shows a liquid of given density flowing steadily in horizontal tube of varying cross-section. Cross-sectional areas at $A$ is $1 . 5{cm}^{2},$ and $B$ is $25{mm}^{2},$ if the speed of liquid at $B$ is $60cm{s}^{- 1}$ then $( {P}_{A} – {P}_{B} )$ is

(Given ${P}_{A}$ and ${P}_{B}$ are liquid pressures at $A$ and $B$ points.

Density $ρ = 1000kg{m}^{- 3}$

$A$ and $B$ are on the axis of tube)
questions.solution:
Using Bernoulli's theorem,

${P}_{A} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{A}^{2} = {P}_{B} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{B}^{2} . . . ( i )$

Using equation of continuity,

${A}_{A}{V}_{A} = {A}_{B}{V}_{B}$

So, $1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4} \times {V}_{A} = 25 \times {10}^{- 6} \times {V}_{B}$

${V}_{A} = \dfrac{25 \times {10}^{- 6}}{1 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}} \times 0 . 6$

$= \dfrac{1}{10}m{s}^{- 1}$

Substituting in equation (i)

$⇒ {P}_{A} - {P}_{B} = \dfrac{1000}{2}\left[0 . {6}^{2} - 0 . {1}^{2}\right] = \dfrac{1000}{2} \times 0 . 7 \times 0 . 5$

$= 175Pa$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as

Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : A spherical body of radius $( 5 \pm 0 . 1 ) mm$ having a particular density is falling through a liquid of constant density. The percentage error in the calculation of its terminal velocity is $4 %$.

Reason R : The terminal velocity of the spherical body falling through the liquid is inversely proportional to its radius. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity is

${V}_{T} = \dfrac{2}{9}{r}^{2}g\dfrac{\left(ρ - {ρ}^{'}\right)}{η} ⇒ {V}_{T} ∝ {r}^{2}$

Differentiating and dividing by ${V}_{T}$,

$⇒ \dfrac{d{V}_{T}}{{V}_{T}} = 2\dfrac{dr}{r} = 2 \times \dfrac{0 . 1}{5}$

So, the percentage error is

$\dfrac{d{V}_{T}}{{V}_{T}} \times 100 = \dfrac{0 . 2}{5} \times 100 = 4 %$

As can be seen the terminal velocity is directly proportional to the square of the radius. Hence $A$ is true but $R$ is false.

questions.q: Speed of a transverse wave on a straight wire (mass $6.0g,$ length $60cm$ and area of cross-section $1.0m{m}^{2}$  is $90{ms}^{- 1}$. If the Young's modulus of wire is $16 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{- 2}$, the extension of wire over its natural length is:

$v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}}$
$⇒ T = \mu{v}^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{\mu{v}^{2}}{A} = Y\dfrac{∆ l}{l}$
$⇒ ∆ l = \dfrac{\mu{v}^{2}l}{AY}$
After substituting value of $\mu, v, l, A$ and $Y$ we get
$∆ l = 0 . 3mm$

questions.q:
The area of cross section of the rope used to lift a load by a crane is $2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}{m}^{2}$. The maximum lifting capacity of the crane is $10$ metric tons. To increase the lifting capacity of the crane to 25 metric tons, the required area of cross section of the rope should be
(take $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$)
questions.solution:
Since breaking stress (Maximum lifting capacity) is the property of material, so it will remain same.

Now, breaking stress$= \dfrac{Maximumliftingcapacity}{Areaofcrosssectionofrope}$

$⇒ \dfrac{10}{2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 4}} = \dfrac{25}{A}$

$A = 625 \times {10}^{- 6}$

$= 6 . 25 \times {10}^{- 4}{m}^{2}$

When two wires are connected end to end, the tension in them will be same.

Change in length using Hooke's law can be found as,

questions.q: Under isothermal condition, the pressure of a gas is given by $P = a{V}^{– 3},$ where $a$ is a constant and $V$ is the volume of the gas. The bulk modulus at constant temperature is equal to
questions.solution:
The data given is

$P = a{V}^{- 3}$

Bulk modulus is given by,

$B = - \dfrac{dP}{\dfrac{dV}{V}} = - V\dfrac{dP}{dV}$

$= - V\dfrac{d}{dV}\left\{\dfrac{a}{{V}^{3}}\right\}$

$= - V\left[\dfrac{- 3a}{{V}^{4}}\right]$

$= \dfrac{3a}{{V}^{3}} = 3P$

questions.q: The point $A$ moves with a uniform speed along the circumference of a circle of radius $0 . 36m$ and covers $30 °$ in $0 . 1s$. The perpendicular projection $P$ from $A$ on the diameter $MN$ represents the simple harmonic motion of $P$. The restoration force per unit mass when $P$ touches $M$ will be :
questions.solution:
The point $A$ covers $30 °$ in $0 . 1s$.
Then, we have $\dfrac{\pi}{6}rad ⟶ 0 . 1s$.
Or $1rad ⟶ \dfrac{0 . 1}{\dfrac{\pi}{6}}s$
Or $2\piin \to \dfrac{0 . 1 \times 6}{\pi} \times 2\pi$
Thus, time taken is $T = 1 . 2sec .$

We know that $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$
Then, $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{1 . 2}$
Restoration force $( F ) = {m \omega}^{2}A .$

Then Restoration force per unit mass $\left(\dfrac{F}{m}\right) = {\omega}^{2}A$
$\left(\dfrac{F}{m}\right) = {\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{1 . 2}\right)}^{2} \times 0 . 36$

$≅ 9 . 87N$

questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion between $x = – A\text{and}x = + A$. If time taken by particle to go from $x = 0$ to $\dfrac{A}{2}$ is $2s$; then time taken by particle in going from $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ to $A$ is:
questions.solution:
The position of a particle performing an SHM is given by:

$x = Asin ( \omegat + ϕ )$

Since at $t = 0s$, the particle is at $x = 0$, therefore the initial phase $ϕ = 0$.

At time $t = 2s$, the particle is at $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$.

$∴ \dfrac{A}{2} = Asin\left(2\omega\right) ⇒ \omega = \dfrac{\pi}{12}{s}^{- 1}$

Therefore, time period

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega} = 24s$

The total time taken from $x = 0$ to $x = A$ is $\dfrac{T}{4} = 6s$.

Since the time taken from $x = 0$ to $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ is $2s$, therefore the time taken from $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ to $x = A$ is $4s$.

questions.q: For particle $P$ revolving round the centre $O$ with radius of circular path $r$ and regular velocity $\omega$, as shown in below figure, the projection of $OP$ on the $x$-axis at time $t$ is
questions.solution:
As can be seen from the diagram, the initial phase of the particle is given by

$\begin{cases}\phi & = & 30 ° \\ & = & \dfrac{\pi}{6}\end{cases}$

The equation of motion of the particle at its initial position at time $t = 0$ can be written as

$x\left(t\right) = rcos\theta . . . ( 1 )$

where, $\theta$ is the angular displacement of the particle at time $t = t$.

Since, the position of the particle at a later instant of time always lags behind its initial position at time $t = 0$, the equation of motion of the particle at any instant of time is given by

$x\left(t\right) = rcos\left(\theta + \phi\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) to obtain the required expression

$x ( t ) = rcos\left(\omegat + \dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

questions.q: A transverse wave is represented by $y = 2sin\left(\omegat - kx\right)cm$. The value of wavelength (in $cm$) for which the wave velocity becomes equal to the maximum particle velocity, will be
questions.solution:
The given equation is $y = 2sin\left(\omegat - kx\right)$

The maximum particle velocity $= A\omega$

And the wave velocity $= \dfrac{\omega}{k}$

For wave velocity to be equal to maximum particle velocity

$\dfrac{\omega}{k} = A\omega$

$⇒ k = \dfrac{1}{A}$

Since, $k = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}$

$\lambda = 2\piA = 4\picm$.

questions.q: The velocity of sound in a gas, in which two wavelengths $4 . 08m$ and $4 . 16m$ produce $40$ beats in $12s$, will be
questions.solution:
If the velocity of the sound in the medium is $v$ then, ${f}_{1} = \dfrac{v}{4 . 08}$ and ${f}_{2} = \dfrac{v}{4 . 16}$

Now beat frequency,

${f}_{b} = \Deltaf = \left|{f}_{1} - {f}_{2}\right| = \dfrac{40}{12} = \dfrac{10}{3}Hz ⇒ v\left[\dfrac{1}{4 . 08} - \dfrac{1}{4 . 16}\right] = \dfrac{10}{3}Hz ⇒ 707 . 2m{s}^{- 1}$
